queue.ShutDown requires Python 3.13
queue.ShutDown and Queue.shutdown() only exist in Python 3.13+. On older runtimes, `except queue.ShutDown` raises AttributeError when evaluated, and q.shutdown() fails (only logged). Workers block forever on get() and never exit.

Worker blocks forever on get() after shutdown flag
work_queue.get() blocks without a timeout; the shutdown flag is only checked between items. Without a working queue shutdown, workers never exit. Also, if shutdown(immediate=False) raises ShutDown on get in the finally path, work_item is unbound.

Failed processing still marks offset complete, causing data loss
The finally block completes the offset even when result_processor raised, so failed messages are committed and never retried, contradicting the 'only commits after successful processing' claim. The test expecting no commit after an error contradicts this behavior.

hash() of str is not stable across processes
Python's string hash is randomized per process (PYTHONHASHSEED), so group-to-queue assignment differs between consumer processes and restarts. Ordering is only guaranteed within one process; use a stable hash (e.g., crc32).

No backpressure; unbounded queues
Queues are unbounded and submit() never blocks or raises MessageRejected, so the docstring's 'natural backpressure' is false. A slow processor leads to unbounded memory growth, and offsets stay uncommitted.

Commit loop races with rebalance and commits from a non-consumer thread
The commit function is called from a background thread, not the Arroyo main thread, and tracker state is never cleared on partition revocation. After rebalance, stale offsets may be committed for partitions no longer owned. Also, the loop runs one more commit pass after shutdown is set.

Committable computation breaks when the first offset is not contiguous with last_committed, and is O(range)
Offsets are only committable if contiguous from last_committed+1 (or min offset on first run). Compacted/filtered offsets or gaps in a partition (e.g., messages skipped by Kafka transactions) block commits forever. The per-offset range scan is also costly.

Non-atomic lock creation / unsynchronized dict access
partition_locks.get followed by setdefault is fine in CPython, but all_offsets/outstanding defaultdicts are mutated (key creation) outside any global lock while get_committable_offsets iterates keys, risking races on first-time partition creation.

Queue pool created in factory __init__ and shared across strategy instances
The pool and its threads are created eagerly in the constructor and shared by all strategies created on rebalance. Each rebalance creates a new SimpleQueueProcessingStrategy whose close() shuts down the shared pool, so subsequent strategies use dead queues.
